task.title: Pin the content of the web client's fallback card view
task.description:
The web client's fallback card view (underivedView, internal/webui/assets/index.html ~:7596) renders a card for exactly one poll when a task is deleted by another clone mid-drag (the crash fix from PR #89). Its deliberate content choices -- the full task ID as the prefix, NO dependency row (the client cannot know which dependencies are done, so "0 of 3" over three finished ones would be a worse lie than one blank poll), and no assignment chips -- are pinned by nothing.

Verified during PR #89's review: replacing the function body with garbage (idPrefix "", dependenciesTotal 9, waitingOnDependencies true) leaves the entire internal/webui suite green, because the Node-harness fixtures make the fallback indistinguishable from the derived view.

Fix: extend TestHandlerClientSurvivesATaskDeletedMidDrag (now internal/webui/unknown_status_recovery_test.go ~:254) with assertions on the fallback card's rendered content during the one-poll window: full-ID prefix shown, no dependency row present, no assignment chips. Test-only change; no production code.

Edge case: reaching the fallback at all requires a task deleted by another clone while its card is mid-drag in this browser.

## Since the conditional poll (PR #181)

The board now polls with If-None-Match, and an unchanged board answers 304 without a redraw. The "exactly one poll" window still holds, but it now depends on one line: the confirmation puts the deleted task back into the model through replaceProjectedTask (index.html ~:7651), which sets `boardValidator = null`, so the next poll sends no tag, gets a full 200, and takes the card away. Without that line the server's document would be unchanged, every poll would be a 304, and the fallback card would stay on the board indefinitely.

So the test should also pin the end of the window against an ETag-honoring fake server (conditionalPollProgram in internal/webui/conditional_poll_client_test.go serves tags and 304s like the real route): after the confirmation, the next poll carries no If-None-Match and the fallback card is gone. Removing `boardValidator = null` from replaceProjectedTask should turn that test red.
